title: Reachable depths for fixed bond size
claim: For every fixed support budget k, the depths admitting a K1-K3 bond of size 3 through k from a top port to an own variable on the repeated first-child branch form an effectively ultimately periodic set. Exact finite-profile saturation allows arbitrary finite auxiliary observations throughout the infinite pattern, including side branches and beyond the target; hence existence at every depth is decidable for fixed k.
standard_statement: Construct the finite algebra of exact projected relations on ports and at most k-1 injectively placed observation labels; saturate arbitrary finite placements, then iterate a deterministic target-depth profile vector and apply the exact K1-K3 acceptance filter on distinct variable identities.
prior_work: Regular tree types and unary finite automata are classical. Compare NEST-COUNT for a fixed top window and BONDS-AND-COUNT E for one concrete growth example. Give an elementary construction that handles finite marking at unbounded side depth and arbitrary supports beyond the target.

validation.status: Final replay passed for 9 primary controls, concrete SAT comparisons, K1–K3, coherent and empty alias behavior, both budget orbits for the predecessor, and negative resource-limit tests.
validation.independence: Finite relation profile algebra versus a separate concrete SAT expansion/projection path, authored in the same task; uniform theorem argued in prose

foundation_claim_scope: Finite projected K1-K3 supports of size at least three in supplied recursive NAE systems, with exact identity and endpoint conventions. No finite-flip source or native contact-composition claim.
scope_limits: The unknown uniform support budget question exists k for all depths is not decided by this proof.
No practical runtime guarantee is given for the 664-rule corpus; this leaf does not repeat its census.
The canonical finite-projection knot-bond test does not settle finite-flip sources at an infinite solution.
failure_conditions: Finite observations are replaced by a depth cutoff before exact profile closure.
The target-vector recurrence drops side branches or continuations beyond the target.
Repeated formal ports are counted as distinct actual variables or equal values are treated as identity.
An empty relation, full relation, or two-variable tie passes the bond filter.
A resource-limited or unrepeated target orbit is reported as a decision.
The branch convention or usual-limit preprocessing differs from the supplied presentation.
